objective: Replace the in-memory SafeCANBus placeholder with a bounded CAN Wire V1 DeviceAdapter hosted by the unified DeviceRuntime; fail closed on malformed frames, timeouts, link faults, and lifecycle races.
acceptance: Construction injects a small transport port and monotonic clock without opening hardware; explicit start and shutdown delegate lifecycle ownership to DeviceRuntime.

DeviceRuntime is the sole owner of configure/activate/deactivate/cleanup, cancellation, worker join, command/telemetry/health planes, backpressure, and subscriber snapshot dispatch; SafeCANBus is an adapter and its compatibility lifecycle methods delegate to that owner.

The command/ACK, telemetry, and health/provenance planes have independent fixed capacities and observable drops/errors; no adapter-local worker, queue, callback registry, or unbounded fallback exists.

Only immutable Classic CAN standard data frames with a known Wire V1 arbitration ID, DLC 8, valid version, reserved bytes, field registry, direction, and cross-field semantics enter the queue or subscriber boundary.
The outbound queue and subscriber sets are bounded, backpressure and rejection are typed, and STOP preempts queued ordinary commands.

At most one command is in flight; successful dispatch starts a local acknowledgement deadline, retries retain command correlation with bounded retry counts, and exhaustion escalates to a correlated STOP.
STOP acknowledgement timeout, bus-off, and link loss fail closed; ordinary commands remain rejected until an explicit successful transport recovery, and recovery never replays pre-fault traffic.
Duplicate, late, uncorrelated, and malformed responses do not confirm a command or cancel STOP escalation.

Accepted inbound results carry an immutable source/interface/sequence/monotonic-time/wall-time/health/evidence envelope; recovery does not silently reset adapter-ingress ordering, and wall-clock rollback is observable and fail-closed.
Subscribe, unsubscribe, counters, diagnostics, and callback snapshot dispatch are thread-safe; callback exceptions are isolated and recorded without terminating dispatch.

Fake transport and fake-clock tests cover validation, saturation, worker draining, timeout/retry/STOP escalation, duplicate and late acknowledgements, callback mutation/failure, shutdown, bus-off, and controlled recovery.
Documentation labels fake transport evidence as host adapter behavior only, not SocketCAN, physical CAN, MCU, actuator, or hard-real-time evidence.
evidence: Focused fake transport and fake-clock regression output.

stop_conditions: The implementation requires changing frozen logical protocol or CAN Wire V1 identifiers, payload layouts, schemas, or canonical models.
The implementation requires kernel wbcan, firmware, robot control, or a concrete SocketCAN dependency.
The adapter would need to claim physical CAN delivery, MCU acceptance, stopped state, or real-time deadline evidence from queueing or fake transport behavior.
An unbounded queue, subscriber collection, retry path, diagnostic store, or shutdown wait is required.
A second adapter-local lifecycle, worker, queue, callback registry, or cancellation model would be needed outside DeviceRuntime.
A write outside allowed_paths is required.
